arxiv-1812-05914.title: End to End Video Segmentation for Driving : Lane Detection For Autonomous Car Conference: Penn State Deep Learning Fall 2018; Fall 2018; State College, PA, USA
arxiv-1812-05914.creator: Tejas Mahale Chaoran Chen and Wenhui Zhang * equal contribution
arxiv-1812-05914.description: Abstract . Safety and decline of road traffic accidents remain important issues of autonomous driving. Statistics show that unintended lane departure is a leading cause of worldwide motor vehicle collisions, making lane detection the most promising and challenge task for self-driving. Today, numerous groups are combining deep learning techniques with computer vision problems to solve self-driving problems.

arxiv-2004-14031.title: A generalized kernel machine approach to identify higher-order composite effects in multi-view datasets
arxiv-2004-14031.creator: Md Ashad Alam, Chuan Qiu, Hui Shen, Yu-Ping Wang, Hong-Wen Deng
arxiv-2004-14031.description: Abstract In recent years, comprehensive study of multi-view datasets (e.g., multi-omics and imaging scans) has been a focus and forefront in biomedical research. State-of-the-art biomedical technologies are enabling us to collect multi-view biomedical datasets for the study of complex diseases.

arxiv-2211-04795.title: Geretsried, Germany
arxiv-2211-04795.creator: wsmilga@compuserve.com
arxiv-2211-04795.description: Abstract Classical and quantum gravity from relativistic quantum mechanics Walter Smilga August 8, 2026 Abstract It is common practice to describe elementary particles by irreducible unitary representations of the Poincaré group. In the same way, multi-particle systems can be described by irreducible unitary representations of the Poincaré group.

arxiv-2308-05272.title: A Generalized Model for Predicting the Drag Coefficient of Arbitrary Bluff Shaped Bodies at High Reynolds Numbers
arxiv-2308-05272.creator: Yousef M. F. El Hasadi, Johan T. Padding
arxiv-2308-05272.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yousef M. F. El Hasadi, Johan T. Padding. We propose an accurate model for the drag coefficient of arbitrary bluff bodies that is valid for high Reynolds numbers ( R ​ e Re ).

arxiv-2402-16196.title: Combining Machine Learning with Computational Fluid Dynamics using OpenFOAM and SmartSim
arxiv-2402-16196.creator: Tomislav Maric, Mohammed Elwardi Fadeli, Alessandro Rigazzi, Andrew Shao, Andre Weiner
arxiv-2402-16196.description: Abstract This is the accepted preprint of the published article: https://doi.org/10.1007/s11012-024-01797-z , please refer to the published article when citing this work. Combining machine learning (ML) with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) opens many possibilities for improving simulations of technical and natural systems.

arxiv-2402-19430.title: Effective interactions of the open bosonic string via field theory
arxiv-2402-19430.creator: Lucia M. Garozzo, Alfredo Guevara
arxiv-2402-19430.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Lucia M. Garozzo, Alfredo Guevara. We describe a method to extract an effective Lagrangian description for open bosonic strings, at zero transcendentality. The method relies on a particular formulation of its scattering amplitudes derived from color-kinematics duality. More precisely, starting from a ( D ​ F ) 2 + YM (DF)^{2}+\text{YM} quantum field theory, we integrate out all the massive degrees of freedom to generate an expansion in the inverse string tension α ′ \alpha^{\prime} .

arxiv-2406-13010.title: IMSRG with flowing 3 body operators, and approximations thereof
arxiv-2406-13010.creator: S. R. Stroberg, T. D. Morris, B. C. He
arxiv-2406-13010.description: Abstract We explore the impact of retaining three-body operators within the in-medium similarity renormalization group (IMSRG), as well as various approximations schemes. After studying two toy problems, idential fermions with a contact interaction and the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model, we employ the valence-space formulation of the IMSRG to investigate the even- A A carbon isotopes with a chiral two-body potential.

arxiv-2503-23901.title: Existence of periodic solution of a non-autonomous allelopathic phytoplankton model with fear effect
arxiv-2503-23901.creator: Satyam Narayan Srivastava, Alexander Domoshnitsky, Seshadev Padhi, Rana D. Parshad
arxiv-2503-23901.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider a non-autonomous allelopathic phytoplankton competition ODE model, incorporating the influence of fear effects observed in natural biological phenomena. Based on Mawhin’s coincidence degree theory some sufficient conditions for existence of periodic solutions are obtained.

arxiv-2504-18207.title: Gradient Descent as a Shrinkage Operator for Spectral Bias
arxiv-2504-18207.creator: Simon Lucey
arxiv-2504-18207.description: Abstract We generalize the connection between activation function and spline regression/smoothing and characterize how this choice may influence spectral bias within a 1D shallow network. We then demonstrate how gradient descent (GD) can be reinterpreted as a shrinkage operator that masks the singular values of a neural network’s Jacobian.

arxiv-2508-18218.title: On rational and real elements in a class of Lie groups
arxiv-2508-18218.creator: Arunava Mandal and Shashank Vikram Singh
arxiv-2508-18218.description: Abstract . For a class of groups G G over a field 𝔽 \mathbb{F} , including certain Lie groups, Algebraic groups and finite groups, we develop a general method to determine rational and real elements, thereby unifying earlier group-specific results into a wider framework.

pmc-10532133.title: Epidemiology, Ventilation Management and Outcomes of COPD Patients Receiving Invasive Ventilation for COVID-19—Insights from PRoVENT-COVID
pmc-10532133.creator: Athiwat Tripipitsiriwat, Orawan Suppapueng, David M. P. van Meenen, Frederique Paulus, Markus W. Hollmann, Chaisith Sivakorn, Marcus J. Schultz
pmc-10532133.description: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a risk factor for death in patients admitted to intensive care units (ICUs) for respiratory support. Previous reports suggested higher mortality in COPD patients with COVID-19. It is yet unknown whether patients with COPD were treated differently compared to non-COPD patients.

pmc-11434483.title: Use of Molecular Logic Gates for the Tuning of Chemosensor Dynamic Range
pmc-11434483.creator: Orhan Acikgoz, Christopher Abelt, Pil Seok Chae, Takahiro Kusukawa
pmc-11434483.description: Dynamic range is a crucial aspect in the development of fluorescent chemosensors. We aimed to address this issue using molecular logic gates. By creating an AND logic gate with two binding sites for the same type of ion, we increased the dynamic range of a sodium chemosensor while still using the same ionophore.

pmc-12436947.title: Risk factors for treatment resistance among women with postpartum depression
pmc-12436947.creator: Y. Chen, D. Lu
pmc-12436947.description: IntroductionPostpartum depression (PPD) impacts millions of new mothers worldwide, and the challenge of treatment resistance (TR) further hampers recovery prospects. The occurrence of TR in women with PPD and the risk factors for TR remain less studied. Identifying these factors is critical for the precise prediction of treatment responses, enabling tailored interventions and effective management of PPD.

pmc-12444959.title: Farm animal coronaviruses: the solution is in vaccines
pmc-12444959.creator: Olga Kondakova, Anna Tsybina, Ekaterina Evtushenko, Ekaterina Ryabchevskaya, Dmitriy Granovskiy, Angelina Kovalenko, Marina Arkhipenko, Nikolai Nikitin, Olga Karpova
pmc-12444959.description: RNA-containing coronaviruses are widespread in nature and can infect a number of vertebrates. Animals are potential sources of human coronaviruses diseases, and interspecies infection by animal coronaviruses has been recorded several times. Such a transmission may have caused the COVID-19 pandemic.

pmc-12589821.title: Clonorchis sinensis Crude Antigen Suppresses Osteoclast Differentiation via Modulation of the NF‐κB and MAPK Signaling Pathway
pmc-12589821.creator: Lili Tang, Shanshan He, Buguo Ma, Zeli Tang, Tingzheng Zhan, Suyu Xiao, Jilong Wang, Jinmin Zhao, Jiake Xu, Yunliang Shi
pmc-12589821.description: Background Clonorchis sinensis crude antigen (CsCA) is recognized for its immunomodulatory capacity in host‐pathogen interactions and immune‐related pathologies, its direct impact on bone remodeling cells remains underexplored. Although prior studies demonstrate CsCA‐mediated suppression of inflammatory bone formation in ankylosing spondylitis, the specific regulatory effects on osteoclastogenesis and associated molecular mechanisms remain elusive.

pmc-12654707.title: High-Sensitivity Troponin T as a Prognostic Factor of Conventional Echocardiographic Parameters in Cancer Patients: A Prospective Observational Study
pmc-12654707.creator: Svetoslava Elefterova Slavcheva, Sevim Ahmed Shefket, Yana Bocheva, Atanas Angelov
pmc-12654707.description: Background and Objectives: Cardiac injury caused by cancer therapy can be detected early using high-sensitivity cardiac troponins (hs-cTns), and this is crucial for preventing irreversible consequences. Clinically relevant issues regarding hs-cTns in oncologic settings—such as reliable cut-off values, the optimal assessment timeframe, factors influencing their levels, and their prognostic ability in relation to functional echocardiographic parameters—require further investigation.

pmc-13278601.title: Simulation-based training: Assessment of impact on medical students’ performance, confidence in CPR, and patient outcomes – A single-center study
pmc-13278601.creator: J Rizwana Fathima, K Senthil Kumar, T Aarthi, K Gaayathri, Saandhiya Raja
pmc-13278601.description: BACKGROUND:Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is an essential life-saving procedure. Traditional training methods may not sufficiently prepare medical students for real-world emergencies. Simulation-based training offers a high-fidelity, immersive approach to teaching CPR skills. To assess the effectiveness of simulation-based CPR training on medical students’ performance and confidence, and to evaluate its impact on real patient outcomes.

pmc-13491761.title: Does plastic waste present an infection hazard? Current evidence, surveillance challenges and research priorities
pmc-13491761.creator: Patrick Ken Kalonde, Kestern Mkoola, Michael Ormsby, Taonga Mwapasa, Precious Innocent Mastala, Madalitso Mphasa, Katalina Tonthola, Fanuel Meckson Bickton, Peter Nambala, Tony Robertson, Richard S Quilliam, Kondwani Chidziwisano, Tracy Morse, Christopher M Jones, Michelle C Stanton, Peter M Atkinso
pmc-13491761.description: Unmanaged plastic waste is widespread in settings with limited waste collection, yet its contribution to infectious disease risk remains poorly understood. In this review, we synthesise current evidence on the human health implications of plastic waste, with a specific focus on environmentally persistent bacteria that are transmitted to humans through the faecal oral route.
